title: Ordinary direct image for admissible coefficients
statement: Let ell be prime and k a positive-characteristic field of characteristic different from ell. Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring satisfying IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient ell Lambda. Let the schemes and morphisms be separated of finite type over k. For every K on X which is constant-model bounded constructible and of finite Tor amplitude, the ordinary right derived module-object direct image Rf_* K is constant-model bounded constructible and of finite Tor amplitude on Y. This concerns ordinary direct image only.

proof.text: Choose $f=pj$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$ quasi-compact open and $p:Z\to Y$ proper by [def-sfb-compactification-over-field]; [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] keeps $Z$ separated of finite type over $k$. These schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over the Noetherian spectrum of a field, and qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine].

source.place: Paragraph (3), choose a compactification inside the standing setting.

proof.text: First use a canonical coefficient representative. For finite $A$, [lem-sfb-finite-open-direct-image-ctf] gives $Rj_*K\in\Dctf(Z,A)$, including the all-module Tor test. For $\mathcal O_E$, [det-thm-sf-pf-adic-open] gives this directly. For $E$ and the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, apply [lem-sfb-rational-open-direct-image-constructible] and then $\Dbc=\Dctf$ from [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2). The cases $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Q_\ell$ take $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), finite, integral and finite-subextension rational open images; old steps 1--3.

proof.text: For the all-continuous algebraic-closure representative, [lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-open-finiteness] gives bounded constant-model constructibility of $Rj_*K$. Apply [det-sf-comp-continuous-algcl-constructible-tor] on the Noetherian scheme $Z$ to obtain finite Tor amplitude. This uses its own coefficient ring throughout.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open image; retained continuous compatibility case in old step 6(3).

proof.text: Apply [det-sf-comp-proper-admissible-hypotheses] to $p$ and the result of steps 2--3. Its first conclusion gives $Rp_*Rj_*K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ for each canonical representative, including the all-continuous one. [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] supplies the cartesian coefficient identifications for every condensed ring; [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] identifies internal derived images with section-ring module images, so [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies this object with $Rf_*K$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), proper image and ordinary direct-image composition; old steps 4--5 and 6(1),(4).

proof.text: For arbitrary admissible $\Lambda$, take its ring-object isomorphism with a representative supplied by $h\Lambda$. [lem-sfb-condensed-coefficient-iso-constructible], applied in both directions, preserves the input and output $\Dctf$. The pulled-back coefficient changes commute with the cartesian maps by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] and [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Under [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison], scalar restriction retains the same module action; thus [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] identifies the scalar restriction of $Rf_*K$ with the representative-coefficient direct image of the scalar restriction of $K$. Step 4 and the inverse scalar equivalence give the required conclusion.

source.place: Ordinary direct-image assembly, old step 6(4), final coefficient-isomorphism transport.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open/proper assembly, retaining the distinct all-continuous coefficient obligation from the existing item.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q59-076465a82 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Re-split of lem-sfb-admissible-direct-image (2026-10-21 human note) meets the rule. Two statement-only new nodes, each a separate substantial argument. lem-sfb-finite-open-direct-image-ctf: the finite-A open image with a uniform Tor interval [a,b+d_j] over the arbitrary standing field. It carries all of old step 1/6(2): descent, Deligne finiteness, the cd bound, the projection formula, the arbitrary-field Tor criterion and the pro-étale comparison. lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-open-finiteness: Dbc for the all-continuous C(−,Q̄_ℓ) ring. This obligation is genuine because C(S,Q̄_ℓ) ≠ colim C(S,E) in the ℓ-adic topology (BS Ex. 7.1.7). The other old arguments go to existing nodes whose statements are exactly their conclusions: O_E to det-thm-sf-pf-adic-open; E and finite-subextension Q̄_ℓ to lem-sfb-rational-open-direct-image-constructible plus ctf=bc(2); proper to clause 1 of det-sf-comp-proper-admissible-hypotheses, which explicitly covers the continuous ring. The old Rf_! sentence was off-statement and old step 6 was a duplicate docstring, so nothing was summarised away. The item is a 5-step assembly of 2409 characters. I checked every step's hypotheses: the compactification lemma, Noetherian/qcqs, the 7 Lean representatives of IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient, the cartesian square needed by ring-sheaf-change-adjunction (sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change plus alpha-iso), and the internal-versus-ringed comparison needed for the pushforward composition. No cycle. Small cases checked: zero ring, U=X, U=∅, G_m⊂A¹. Batch-5 flags are generic and accepted: lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization and lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison are internal-versus-section module comparisons, already reached by the base through det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational; lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact is exactness of a geometric inverse image. Neither is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality. Tool uses to record: det-thm-sf-pf-adic-open, lem-sfb-rational-open-direct-image-constructible, det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc, lem-sfb-alpha-iso, lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison, lem-sfb-condensed-coefficient-iso-constructible. Advisory: lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves already gives the Dbc half of the finite node, and its future proof should cite it. The parent's created.item is a Lean module name, which is why both new nodes carry from.node null.
